Second SFI (Grade R, Term 1, Emergent Reading / Phonological-Phonemic Awareness) is an auditory discrimination standard: 'Distinguishes aurally between different sounds especially at the beginning of own name' (LC tags: listening, name, phonemic awareness, sounds). Both are Grade R emergent-literacy skills that use the learner's own name as the anchoring text, giving complementary reading-side (hearing initial sounds in the name) and writing-side (tracing the name's letter forms) coherence. However, the nominated overlap is otherwise generic (shared tokens 'of', 'own', 'the'; shared LC tag field 'name'; shared Grade R ancestor only; LC Jaccard ~0.10), and the two skills operate in distinct modalities and Skill Areas, so proficiency in aural sound discrimination does not substantively support success in motor tracing (or vice versa). Term 1 to Term 4 ordering would permit second_to_first, but there is no pair-specific developmental dependency to justify it, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Same-rank, same-term development would require substantive pair-specific extension evidence, which is absent, and the direction would in any case be ambiguous. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Skills (rank 0) but sit in different skill areas and sub-strands: the first is Term 2 EMERGENT WRITING / Handwriting ('Begins to form letters using finger painting, paint brushes, wax crayons', LC tags handwriting, letter formation, crayons), the second is Term 3 EMERGENT READING / Relates sounds to letters and words ('Recognises aurally and visually some initial consonants and vowels... points to the h that it says /h/', LC tags phonics, initial sounds, letter-sound, consonants, vowels).
